review_candidates.title: Member of Technical Staff - Robotics Lab (Remote)
review_candidates.description: Role: Member of Technical Staff - Robotics Lab (Remote) Location: Remote (Work from Anywhere) Job Type: Full-Time Payout: $400K - $1500K/yr Role Overview: We are hiring for one of our clients, seeking a Member of Technical Staff (Robotics Lab) to work on a full-time basis. The role involves designing, developing, and deploying robotics systems with a focus on scalable autonomy and real-time control. Candidates will collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate hardware and software solutions for next-generation robotic platforms. Key Responsibilities: • Design and implement control algorithms for robotic systems, including kinematics, dynamics, and path planning. • Develop and maintain software for robot perception, localization, and mapping using sensor fusion techniques. • Collaborate with hardware engineers to integrate sensors, actuators, and embedded systems into functional robotic prototypes. • Optimize robotic performance for efficiency, reliability, and safety in dynamic environments. • Document technical specifications, test results, and deployment procedures for internal and external stakeholders. Required Skills & Qualifications: • Proficiency in robotics frameworks such as ROS, ROS 2, or similar platforms. • Strong programming skills in C++, Python, or other relevant languages for robotics applications. • Experience with real-time control systems, embedded software, and hardware-in-the-loop testing. • Knowledge of computer vision, SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping), or sensor fusion techniques. • Familiarity with simulation tools like Gazebo, CoppeliaSim, or NVIDIA Isaac Sim is required. • Experience with robotic operating systems, middleware, and communication protocols (e.g., CAN, Ethernet, UDP). • Ability to design and analyze algorithms for motion planning, obstacle avoidance, and task execution. • Experience with version control systems such as Git and collaborative software development workflows. • Understanding of machine learning techniques for robotics, including reinforcement learning or imitation learning. • Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to troubleshoot complex robotic systems. More About the Opportunity: This role offers a unique opportunity to work with a global leader in the Information Services industry, contributing to the development of autonomous robotic systems for industrial and commercial applications. The position involves high-impact work with cutting-edge technology and the chance to shape the future of robotics in a fast-evolving field. Equal Opportunity Employer: We hire based on skills and expertise. All qualified candidates are welcome regardless of background, experience, or prior employment history. Applications are reviewed solely on demonstrated technical ability and qualifications. Apply Now!

review_candidates.title: Community mobilizer
review_candidates.description: Company Description IOM, the International Organization for Migration, is the leading intergovernmental organization dedicated to promoting humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. Working closely with governments, partners, and communities, IOM supports migrants and displaced populations through protection, assistance, and sustainable solutions. The organization focuses on community-based approaches that strengthen resilience, social cohesion, and access to essential services. With operations around the world, IOM offers staff the opportunity to contribute to meaningful, people-centered work in complex humanitarian and development contexts. Role Description The Community Mobilizer is a full-time, on-site role based in Chattogram, Bangladesh. The role involves engaging with community members on a daily basis to understand their needs, encourage participation in IOM programs, and support the implementation of community-based activities. The Community Mobilizer will organize meetings, focus group discussions, and awareness sessions, ensuring clear communication about available services and initiatives. The role includes building trust with diverse community groups, collecting feedback, and sharing information with IOM teams to improve program quality and relevance. The Community Mobilizer will collaborate closely with colleagues, local leaders, and partner organizations to strengthen social cohesion and promote inclusive, safe community spaces. Qualifications Strong Interpersonal Skills and Communication abilities to build trust and maintain constructive dialogue with diverse community members. Experience in Community Engagement and Community Management to plan, facilitate, and follow up on community-based activities and initiatives. Customer Service orientation, including responsiveness, patience, and the ability to handle sensitive inquiries with respect and empathy. Knowledge of local context in Chattogram and surrounding areas, including cultural norms and community structures. Ability to work on-site in field settings, often in challenging environments, while maintaining professionalism and safety awareness. Basic skills in data collection, reporting, and documentation of community feedback and activity outcomes. Prior experience in humanitarian, development, or social work settings is an asset. Relevant education or training in social sciences, community development, or a related field is preferred.

review_candidates.title: Community Builder
review_candidates.description: Location:  Mauritius Reports to: Marketing Lead  Contract: [Permanent / Fixed-term], part-time or full-time available, hybrid  Salary: Rs 20,000 – 30,000 (based on experience), part-time pro-rated  Applications close: 15th September 2026 The job : The Good Shop is a social enterprise, not a charity in the traditional sense. We run 4 second-hand shops, and use the revenue to fund inclusive employment opportunities and scholarships. This is why we're hiring a Community Builder — not a typical Community Manager. The role goes beyond social media: you'll be running programmes with local content creators, Good Shop employees, our partners and their teams, our donors, and other activists — creating fresh content with them along the way, not about them from behind a desk. The three core skills we need: 1. Proactive project manager You set goals and deadlines and work with multiple stakeholders to deliver projects on time — whether that's a donation drive, communications support, a campaign, or an event. 2. Ecosystem builder You build and nurture relationships across the impact sector, engaging a wide range of stakeholders. This is a people-first, out-in-the-field role — not one spent behind a desk. 3. Communication operator You own communications end to end: writing briefs, designing presentations, building a funnel, drafting social posts, managing budgets, shooting video, boosting content, reporting on results, and training others. You bring your own frameworks for how you work — we're not looking for someone who needs one built for them. What matters beyond skills We're looking for genuine passion for impact. As an inclusive workplace, we communicate in Creole, English, and sign language. Fluency in Creole and English is expected for this role; sign language is a valuable bonus, not a requirement. The practical details: Flexible position: open to part-time and hybrid arrangements — but expect frequent in-person meetings, given the nature of the work. Experience: open Education: open Start date: 1st of October How we hire: Applications close 15th September 2026 . 10 candidates will be contacted on 18th September  and asked to present a campaign proposal on 21st September. Each will receive a Rs 500 voucher from The Good Shop as compensation for their time. 3 selected candidates will be invited to a final interview with our Managing Director on the 25th of September and a decision provided on 28th of September.
